### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fa95f888a9d0d0eb062c040098783b0e90ad3dc1` — the merge of head `b5a2e4481114333fcc08b034aecd28d6a4428af9` into base `2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fa95f888a9d0d0eb062c040098783b0e90ad3dc1 && git checkout fa95f888a9d0d0eb062c040098783b0e90ad3dc1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4 b5a2e4481114333fcc08b034aecd28d6a4428af9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4 && git merge --no-ff b5a2e4481114333fcc08b034aecd28d6a4428af9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b5a2e4481114333fcc08b034aecd28d6a4428af9`
Local-runs: none

Isolated reviewer for PR #21036 (card #20918). Inputs: the card body and its four comments (triage `5918567230`, the claim, the dev report `5923712419`, the seat ACCEPT), the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` at the head (`2f2fa11d7..b5a2e4481`, 9 files, +535 / -29), and the check-runs on the head. Source cited below was read from the head's tree objects, nothing was built or run.

**Check-runs on the head:** 34, all completed — 31 success, 3 skipped (Build Docs and Console Pin Gate are path-filtered, Packed-tarball smoke is opt-in), 0 failure, 0 pending. The required contexts (TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard) and Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, the four Type Check jobs and the claim guards are all success.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set, engine-aggregate (ObjectQL) path — WIDENED, judged right.** The only production change is `ObjectQLStrategy.convertFilter`: the `set` leaf becomes `{ $null: false }` (was `{ $ne: null }`) and the `notSet` leaf `{ $null: true }` (was the bare `null`). `driver-sql`'s `assertOperatorAppliesToColumn` throws only for an op in `JSON_COLUMN_INCOMPATIBLE_OPERATORS` (`$eq`, `$ne`, the ordering family, `$in`, `$nin`, `$between`); `$null` and `$exists` are absent from it. So on a multi-valued lookup's JSON column, every filter the `where` door lowers to those leaves — a `$not` operand's guard (#5146), the `$notContains` escape (#5298), an author's own `$null` / `$exists` — goes from `400 INVALID_FILTER` to rows, at the cube read, the dataset door's `selection.runtimeFilter`, and a dataset measure's `filter`. That is a widening of what the door accepts on one strategy, and the declaration says `yes`. Right.
2. **"The engine's own spelling" — right.** `lowerFilterCondition` rule 3 (`guardNullPolarity`, `packages/spec/src/data/filter-lowering.ts`) emits `{ f: { $null: false } }` for the `requireValue` arm and `{ $or: [{ f: { $null: true } }, { f: spec }] }` for `allowNull`; the engine runs it on every driver at `resolveThenLowerWhere` (`engine.ts:1204`). `operatorIsNullTotal('$null')` is true, so the engine reads the strategy's guard as already total and adds none beside it. The dev's "three guards, then two" reading is consistent with source; it was not re-measured here.
3. **Previously-answered queries — spelling-only, no narrowing, judged right.** On single-valued columns `driver-sql` compiles `$ne` with a null comparand as `whereNotNull(field)` and `$null: false` as `whereNotNull(field)`; `$eq null` / the bare null compile IS NULL and `$null: true` as `whereNull(field)` — one predicate either way. The ten re-judged cases in five pins (`filter-normalizer-not-null-safe`, `filter-value-type-fidelity`, `objectql-contains-canonical-operator`, `objectql-daterange`, `where-boolean-flag-refusal`): read in the diff, every change is to an `engine:` expectation or to a stand-in engine's reader of the new shape; every `rows:` table and every id expectation is unchanged. The native strategy (`native-sql-strategy.ts`), the `/analytics/sql` echo and the read scope (reaches the engine without `convertFilter`) are untouched by the diff.
4. **Rows 8-9 (`{ owners: { $ne: null } }` and the bare `{ owners: null }`) — a widening already covered by `yes`, declared, acceptable; not a divergence that blocks.** At the analytics door these are null predicates by contract (#5332: `fieldLeaves` reads `$eq` / `$ne` with a null comparand as `notSet` / `set`, and `raw === null` as `notSet`). The native strategy answered them before; the ObjectQL strategy now answers the same rows, and those rows are exactly what the engine answers for the equivalent `$null` spelling (rows 5 and 7: a, b, c, d and e). `engine.find` refuses the `$ne` / bare spelling only because the #7398 gate reads the operator, not the comparand — a fail-closed refusal, not a different answer. The changeset body states the difference ("One difference from the engine remains"), no driver file is touched, and triage's ⛔ on a driver special case is honoured. No new card owed.
5. **Public surface — unchanged, right.** No export added or removed; `packages/spec`, `packages/objectql`, `packages/drivers` untouched (the 9 files are the changeset, one `packages/rest/src/*.test.ts`, and `packages/services/service-analytics/src/**`). No REST route, query-parameter set, error code or schema moved.
6. **Triage's direction — honoured.** Route one of the either/or ("the guard in a form `driver-sql` applies") with the measured reason that rows 5-7 carry no guard and "stop adding the guard" would leave them refused; `filter-normalizer.ts` untouched. Pins: the rest pin runs both compositions (native and engine-aggregate) over the shipped `SecurityPlugin` + `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` chain against `engine.find` as the reference, with the single-valued control; the unit pin adds the engine-input spelling assertion. As triage asked.
7. **Non-SQL drivers — reasoning, not measurement, recorded as such.** The engine's lowering already hands every driver `$null` guards on every `$not`; `driver-mongodb`'s `$null` arm translates to `$eq: null` / `$ne: null`, and `driver-memory` / `driver-turso` carry a `$null` arm. Consistent; not a measured row.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/20918-objectql-not-multivalue-served.md`: `@objectstack/service-analytics` **`minor`**, body carries `Clause-②: yes`. PR body line 2: `Clause-②: yes`, no arm. `Check Changeset` success on the head.
- **Grammar — right.** `yes` with no arm declares a widening (`yes` and `yes (widening)` are one reading). A `(narrowing)` arm is not owed: no previously-answered row moved (① item 3). No `(widening)` arm is required.
- **Level — right.** `yes` takes at least `minor`; one published package grew its accept set; nothing breaks, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed and none is written.
- **Prose — accurate against the diff.** It names the two doors, the strategy, the filter shapes that went from 400 to rows, what is unchanged, and the one remaining difference from the engine.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the dev report.
- **Deviation — five existing pin files edited (claim named new files only):** verified in the diff as spelling-only (① item 3); none is a file of #20912 (`structured-json-dimension-door.ts`, `dataset-compiler.ts`, `analytics-service.ts`) or #20889 (`native-sql-strategy.ts`, `aggregate-answer.ts`, `driver-sql`). Accepted.
- **Deviation — G3 wording ("excludes NULL rows") and the `:1872` vs `:1920` location:** source confirms rule 3 makes the negation answer the NULL row; the location is a nit. Accepted.
- **Deviation — rest `local` suite narrowed to the 16 analytics pins; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED:** closed by the check-runs on the head (Test Core 6 of 6 shards, Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, the four Type Check jobs — all success).
- **Out-of-scope 1 — rows 8-9:** judged in ① item 4; acceptable, declared; no card owed.
- **Out-of-scope 2 — `engine.aggregate`'s per-aggregation filter counting 5 where `engine.find` counts 3:** evidence for #20873 (`domain:engine`, open), the neighbour triage kept separate. Not folded here. Accepted.
- **Out-of-scope 3 — an external object's datetime column on `driver-sql`'s legacy-repair path, NOT MEASURED:** read at source, `driver-sql`'s `$null` arm compiles `whereNull` / `whereNotNull` on the raw column, and the driver's own comment on that path says a legacy-repair expression is NULL exactly when the column is; the engine's own guards already take that arm under `engine.find`. Nothing shown defective; it stays unmeasured, no card owed, no block.
- **NOT MEASURED — PostgreSQL and MySQL:** `$null` compiles through knex's dialect-neutral `whereNull` / `whereNotNull`; Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) is success on the head, though that lane does not necessarily run this pin. Left as CI-owned, recorded as reasoning.
- **Dispatch surface:** `filter-normalizer.ts`, `packages/drivers/**`, `packages/objectql/src/**`, `packages/spec/src/**` all untouched, as the claim required. No label other than the assignee written; a changeset is present, so no `skip-changeset`.
- **Red-first and ablation counts (A0 16 red, A1 7 / 2, A2 13 / 3):** the dev's own readings, not re-run under this read-only shape; this record relies on the head's green check-runs for the current state, and on the diff for the spelling-only claim.
